description: Doris Stanley recounts being 21 and working at an oyster-bar restaurant when television coverage of the September 11 attacks interrupted preparations for lunch. She describes watching repeated footage of the attacks in New York, the Pentagon, and Pennsylvania, including the collapse of a World Trade Center building. Stanley recalls feeling shocked and frightened, and says the footage continued for hours before she asked her boss whether the televisions could be turned off. She connects the experience to later anxiety and panic attacks, fear of heights and bridges, and counseling at UCF, where she says she explored its services and unpacked the experience. Stanley says a later visit to the New York memorial during a conference was healing, and reflects that she felt the loss despite not believing she had personally lost anyone. Recorded for the UCF Remembers 9/11 collection on September 11, 2026, this account centers on television-viewing and its lasting personal effects, rather than physical presence at an attack site.
